speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To understand what is wrong, please tell me: are your stools normal in color and consistency, or do you notice any blood or mucus? Have you been vomiting, and if so, is it projectile or green in color?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: The baby is fussy, feeding poorly, with distension and pain on abdominal palpation. Given the severity of abdominal tenderness and the infant's age, have you noticed any episodes of the baby drawing their knees up or passing episodes of currant-jelly stool?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying; the absence of vomiting, diarrhea, or fever helps narrow the differential. Given the significant abdominal distension and tenderness without signs of infection, have you noticed any visible peristaltic waves or a palpable abdominal mass? Also, has the baby passed any gas or stool recently?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.
